newsitem.title: USA: Highlights of New York State contingency budget.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of New York State contingency budget.

text.p: The New York State Senate and Assembly said they approved a contingency budget to keep the government running through May 9. The state's budget is due on April 1, a deadline that was not expected to be met.
Senate Majority Leader Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, released a summary of the $9.65 billion contingency pact. Highlights of the agreement follow:
--$960 million in General Fund and $1.35 billion in federal funds for Medicaid payments to providers.
--$1.672 billion for the state insurance fund.
--$756 million for the Medical Malpractice Insurance Association.
--$807 million for personal services expenditures for state, legislative, judiciary employees.
--$225 million for nonpersonal service payments for state agencies that lets them enter into contracts after April 1 and incur liabilities up to May 9.
--$838 million for education payments, including $195.4 million for pre-kindergarden handicapped payments covering all outstanding 1995-96 and prior year claims currently approved.
--$239 million for contingency appropriation for Health Insurance Reserve Receipts Fund.

--$140 million for local assistance payments for the Office of Mental Retardation and Development Disabilities, the Office of Alcoholism and Substance Abuse Services, the State Office for the Aging and the Division of Veterans' Affairs.
--$70 million in bad debt and charity care payments.
--$38 million to reimburse social service districts administrative costs.
--$33 million to the Department of Transportation for operating expenses of the Metropolitan Transportation Authority.
